name: Frame-time budget and graceful degradation
summary: Performance remains controllable when each target profile has measured CPU, GPU, memory, IO, and network budgets plus an ordered degradation ladder that preserves authoritative play.
player_action: The player performs the same demanding encounter across supported hardware and quality profiles.
system_response: The game measures frame time by subsystem and removes optional presentation cost before responsiveness, simulation rules, critical cues, or earned state.

conflicts_with: quality settings that alter hidden rules

failure_modes: Average FPS hides repeatable hitches at decision boundaries.
A lower setting removes a critical cue or interaction.
Presentation degradation changes simulation or persistence.
Memory or IO spikes exceed the platform budget despite acceptable steady-state rendering.
accessibility: Preserve cue meaning when effects density, motion, flash, shadows, or audio complexity are reduced.
Test assistive input and output configurations inside the same frame-time matrix.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Replay one instrumented worst-case encounter on the lowest supported profile with every degradation step independently toggleable.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: The accepted target holds its declared budgets and every degradation step preserves decisions, state, and required cues.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Budgets hold only after an expensive layer is removed without a validated replacement.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Any supported profile exceeds budget at a repeatable decision boundary or changes authoritative outcomes.

evidence.claim: Epic documents frame time, target frame rates, CPU/GPU/memory bottlenecks, target-hardware profiling, device profiles, scalability, and frame-by-frame diagnostic tooling.
evidence.notes: Supports explicit per-profile budgets and profiling; this record adds the state-preservation test boundary.
